selectionNote: Curated for topic fit, teaching quality, creator credibility, and public YouTube availability. Videos are optional inputs to proof missions, not LearnByShorts content.

ai-fluency.title: Generative AI in a Nutshell - how to survive and thrive in the age of AI
ai-fluency.creator: Henrik Kniberg
ai-fluency.why: A durable visual mental model for capabilities, prompting, context, and human judgment.
ai-fluency.before: Write your current explanation of how a generative model produces an answer.
ai-fluency.after: Name two useful capabilities, two failure modes, and one decision that must remain human.

ai-fluency.title: Why Large Language Models Hallucinate
ai-fluency.creator: IBM Technology
ai-fluency.why: Connects confident model output to the need for source checks, abstention, and accountable decisions.
ai-fluency.before: Predict three situations in which fluent output could still be wrong.
ai-fluency.after: Add one hallucination test and one human-ownership rule to your verification gate.

agentic-engineering.title: Generative vs Agentic AI: Shaping the Future of AI Collaboration
agentic-engineering.creator: IBM Technology
agentic-engineering.why: Clarifies when a bounded agent is justified and what separates it from a single model response.
agentic-engineering.before: Mark which parts of your target workflow are deterministic, model-driven, or human-approved.
agentic-engineering.after: Revise the boundary so every autonomous step has an explicit stop or escalation condition.

agentic-engineering.title: Observability and Evals for AI Agents: A Simple Breakdown
agentic-engineering.creator: LangChain
agentic-engineering.why: Shows why tool calls need traces and why an agent loop needs task-level evaluation.
agentic-engineering.before: List the inputs, outputs, and failure states you would record for one tool call.
agentic-engineering.after: Add one trace field and two representative failure cases to your agent evaluation set.

ai-product-engineering.title: Is RAG Still Needed? Choosing the Best Approach for LLMs
ai-product-engineering.creator: IBM Technology
ai-product-engineering.why: Frames retrieval as a product and data decision instead of a default architecture.
ai-product-engineering.before: Identify which user answers require current, private, or source-citable information.
ai-product-engineering.after: Document when your product retrieves, answers from model knowledge, or abstains.

ai-product-engineering.title: LLM as a Judge: Scaling AI Evaluation Strategies
ai-product-engineering.creator: IBM Technology
ai-product-engineering.why: Introduces scalable grading while making the case for rubrics and human calibration.
ai-product-engineering.before: Write one outcome a deterministic test can grade and one that needs judgment.
ai-product-engineering.after: Create a small quality scorecard and record where a model grader needs human review.

ai-product-engineering.title: Master Full-Stack Docker & CI/CD – Build a Production-Ready Pipeline
ai-product-engineering.creator: freeCodeCamp.org
ai-product-engineering.why: Provides a concrete path from a working feature to a repeatable, test-gated release.
ai-product-engineering.before: List the checks that must pass before your thin slice can reach users.
ai-product-engineering.after: Add one release gate, one rollback step, and one operational metric to your ship plan.

ai-evals-reliability.title: LLM Evaluation Basics: Datasets & Metrics
ai-evals-reliability.creator: Generative AI at MIT
ai-evals-reliability.why: A concise foundation for turning vague model quality into datasets and observable metrics.
ai-evals-reliability.before: Write one useful, harmful, ambiguous, and abstaining example for your task.
ai-evals-reliability.after: Expand the examples into a versioned test distribution with explicit labels.

ai-evals-reliability.title: LLM as a Judge: Scaling AI Evaluation Strategies
ai-evals-reliability.creator: IBM Technology
ai-evals-reliability.why: Explains model grading tradeoffs and the need to measure agreement with human judgment.
ai-evals-reliability.before: Separate criteria that can be checked deterministically from criteria that require judgment.
ai-evals-reliability.after: Run a small agreement study and document one grader blind spot.

ai-evals-reliability.title: Production Evals For Agentic AI Systems
ai-evals-reliability.creator: AI Engineer
ai-evals-reliability.why: Connects offline evaluation to real production behavior and release decisions.
ai-evals-reliability.before: Choose the quality, safety, latency, and cost thresholds that would block a release.
ai-evals-reliability.after: Compare two versions and record one regression your gate would stop.

ai-assisted-coding.title: Spec-Driven Development: AI Assisted Coding Explained
ai-assisted-coding.creator: IBM Technology
ai-assisted-coding.why: Centers contracts and constrained implementation before asking an AI system to write code.
ai-assisted-coding.before: Write the invariants, interfaces, acceptance checks, and non-goals for one feature.
ai-assisted-coding.after: Tighten the task until another engineer could execute it without guessing.

ai-assisted-coding.title: How to automate code reviews and testing with GitHub Copilot
ai-assisted-coding.creator: GitHub
ai-assisted-coding.why: Demonstrates AI-assisted review as an input to testing and human ownership, not an approval shortcut.
ai-assisted-coding.before: List the boundary, security, concurrency, and failure-state risks in your current diff.
ai-assisted-coding.after: Add one risk-derived test and write which AI suggestion you rejected and why.

full-stack-delivery.title: Master Full-Stack Docker & CI/CD – Build a Production-Ready Pipeline
full-stack-delivery.creator: freeCodeCamp.org
full-stack-delivery.why: Ties a complete application slice to containers, automated checks, and a repeatable delivery pipeline.
full-stack-delivery.before: Sketch the UI, API, validation, storage, and failure boundaries of one vertical slice.
full-stack-delivery.after: Ship the slice through a pipeline that deliberately catches one failure.

full-stack-delivery.title: Docker Tutorial for Beginners [FULL COURSE in 3 Hours]
full-stack-delivery.creator: TechWorld with Nana
full-stack-delivery.why: Builds the runtime vocabulary needed to explain images, containers, networks, volumes, and operations.
full-stack-delivery.before: Write your current distinction between an image, container, volume, and network.
full-stack-delivery.after: Containerize one service and document health, configuration, secrets, and rollback.

data-applied-ml.title: Harvard CS50’s Intro to Databases with SQL – Full University Course
data-applied-ml.creator: freeCodeCamp.org and CS50
data-applied-ml.why: Provides a rigorous SQL foundation for defining grain, querying defensibly, and checking data quality.
data-applied-ml.before: Write the decision, metric, grain, keys, and minimum data needed for your analysis.
data-applied-ml.after: Create one query plus checks for missing values, duplicates, and time-boundary errors.

data-applied-ml.title: But what is a neural network? | Deep learning chapter 1
data-applied-ml.creator: 3Blue1Brown
data-applied-ml.why: A visual foundation that helps learners explain model behavior without hiding behind jargon.
data-applied-ml.before: Sketch how inputs, weights, activations, and outputs might represent your problem.
data-applied-ml.after: Compare the model to a simple baseline and explain the improvement and uncertainty plainly.

backend-distributed-systems.title: Lecture 1: Introduction
backend-distributed-systems.creator: MIT 6.824: Distributed Systems
backend-distributed-systems.why: Establishes the core distributed-systems tradeoffs behind state, consistency, and fault tolerance.
backend-distributed-systems.before: Draw the path of one request and mark every state owner and network boundary.
backend-distributed-systems.after: Choose a consistency model and record one rejected alternative.

backend-distributed-systems.title: Lecture 2: RPC and Threads
backend-distributed-systems.creator: MIT 6.824: Distributed Systems
backend-distributed-systems.why: Grounds retries, concurrency, duplicate requests, and partial failure in concrete RPC behavior.
backend-distributed-systems.before: Predict what happens when a request times out after the server has already acted.
backend-distributed-systems.after: Add idempotency, bounded retry, and recovery behavior to one dependency call.

backend-distributed-systems.title: OpenTelemetry: Simplifying Hybrid Cloud Monitoring
backend-distributed-systems.creator: IBM Technology
backend-distributed-systems.why: Connects logs, metrics, and traces to the path of a real user request.
backend-distributed-systems.before: List the fields needed to correlate one request across service and storage boundaries.
backend-distributed-systems.after: Trace one failure end to end and define the signal that should alert first.

cloud-finops.title: Introduction to AWS Lambda - Serverless Compute on Amazon Web Services
cloud-finops.creator: Amazon Web Services
cloud-finops.why: An official foundation for deciding when event-driven serverless compute is the cheapest adequate shape.
cloud-finops.before: Compare static hosting, serverless functions, containers, and managed services for your traffic profile.
cloud-finops.after: Record the scaling, availability, cold-start, and cost assumptions behind your chosen shape.

cloud-finops.title: Building serverless applications with infrastructure as code
cloud-finops.creator: AWS Events
cloud-finops.why: Shows how repeatable infrastructure and operational signals fit a serverless workload.
cloud-finops.before: List every resource, permission, encryption decision, alarm, and deletion safeguard.
cloud-finops.after: Review a change set and prove that no datastore or credential is public.

cloud-finops.title: Mastering Cloud Cost Optimization with FinOps
cloud-finops.creator: PolarSeven
cloud-finops.why: Turns cloud cost from a monthly surprise into explicit budgets, unit economics, and optimization loops.
cloud-finops.before: Name the usage unit, major cost drivers, and maximum acceptable monthly spend.
cloud-finops.after: Add a budget threshold, anomaly response, and one right-sizing experiment.

platform-engineering-kubernetes.title: Kubernetes Tutorial for Beginners [FULL COURSE in 4 Hours]
platform-engineering-kubernetes.creator: TechWorld with Nana
platform-engineering-kubernetes.why: A strong practical foundation for workloads, configuration, networking, storage, and safe operations.
platform-engineering-kubernetes.before: Map one developer workflow and mark where a container platform reduces or adds friction.
platform-engineering-kubernetes.after: Deploy one workload with health, resources, configuration, and rollback defined.

platform-engineering-kubernetes.title: What are Golden Paths in platform engineering?
platform-engineering-kubernetes.creator: Platform Engineering
platform-engineering-kubernetes.why: Explains why a platform should offer a supported path while preserving escape hatches and measurable value.
platform-engineering-kubernetes.before: Choose one repeated developer task that is costly, inconsistent, or unsafe.
platform-engineering-kubernetes.after: Draft a golden path and define adoption, lead-time, reliability, and satisfaction signals.

secure-engineering.title: Operationalizing AI Supply Chain Security with AIBOM
secure-engineering.creator: OWASP GenAI Security Project
secure-engineering.why: Connects AI-specific attack surfaces to inventory, provenance, abuse boundaries, and operational controls.
secure-engineering.before: List assets, actors, trust boundaries, model dependencies, and the most harmful plausible outcome.
secure-engineering.after: Add one prevention, detection, response, and residual-risk decision for an AI abuse case.

secure-engineering.title: Demystifying end-to-end supply chain security
secure-engineering.creator: GitHub
secure-engineering.why: Covers identity, dependencies, build provenance, and release integrity across the delivery chain.
secure-engineering.before: Map who and what can change source, dependencies, builds, artifacts, and production.
secure-engineering.after: Remove one unnecessary permission and add one verifiable delivery-chain control.

systems-interviews.title: How to Answer System Design Interview Questions (Complete Guide)
systems-interviews.creator: Aced (formerly Exponent)
systems-interviews.why: Provides a structured system-design conversation rather than a memorized architecture dump.
systems-interviews.before: Write the clarifying questions, scale assumptions, and success criteria you would ask first.
systems-interviews.after: Redesign one weak answer and explicitly defend two tradeoffs.

systems-interviews.title: Debugging Like A Pro
systems-interviews.creator: ByteByteGo
systems-interviews.why: Reinforces hypothesis-driven debugging, signal selection, and communicating under uncertainty.
systems-interviews.before: State your first three hypotheses for a failure and what evidence would eliminate each.
systems-interviews.after: Run a timed debugging drill and record where your reasoning became unfocused.

systems-interviews.title: Top 10 Behavioral Software Engineering Interview Questions
systems-interviews.creator: Aced (formerly Exponent)
systems-interviews.why: Helps turn real project evidence into concise, defensible behavioral stories.
systems-interviews.before: Choose one project and list the situation, your decisions, measurable result, and lesson.
systems-interviews.after: Record a full simulation and remove vague claims, team-only credit, and unsupported metrics.
